source.title: Sharpness-diversity tradeoff: improving flat ensembles with SharpBalance
source.authors: Haiquan Lu; Xiao-Tian Liu; Ye-Fan Zhou; Qun Li; Kurt Keutzer; Michael W. Mahoney; Yujun Yan; Huan-Rui Yang; Yao-Qing Yang

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests a trade-off between sharpness and diversity in deep ensembles and reports ensemble ID/OOD accuracy. It does not test the claim versions’ training-versus-test error, memorization of random labels, or the specified magnitude-aware sharpness measure’s relation to the generalization gap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results about sharpness, ensemble diversity, ensemble improvement, and ID/OOD accuracy. These do not measure the behaviors named by the listed versions. Theoretical statements and cited prior work are not extracted as empirical results.
record.test_reason: The study measures sharpness, ensemble diversity, ensemble improvement, and ID/OOD accuracy. It does not measure the training–test gap or compare generalization-measure rankings required by V7, and it does not test V1–V6 or V8. Its adaptive sharpness measure is magnitude-aware, contrary to the record's explanation; the outcome mismatch is what prevents a V7 test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: sharpness minimization reduces ensemble diversity and ensemble improvement, and SharpBalance is proposed to improve this trade-off and ID/OOD performance. Their blanket performance-improvement claim needs qualification: Figure 12 reports lower WRN-40-2 OOD accuracy for SharpBalance than SAM on both datasets.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies sharpness-aware training and ensemble diversity, not the interventions or measurements specified in the claim versions. Its experiments primarily use SAM-trained ensembles and introduce SharpBalance.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported trade-off varies with dataset, model width, model sparsity, and sharpness/diversity metric. Narrower or sparser models show a more pronounced trade-off.

fits_no_version.finding: Lower adaptive sharpness accompanies lower ensemble diversity and ensemble improvement, while individual-member OOD accuracy improves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAM-trained ResNet18 ensembles exhibit a trade-off between member sharpness and ensemble diversity on the tested image datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: The sharpness–diversity trade-off has steeper fitted slopes in narrower and sparser models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Width and sparsity affect the strength of the sharpness–diversity trade-off.

fits_no_version.finding: SharpBalance improves reported ResNet18 ensemble accuracies, but WRN-40-2 corruption accuracy falls below SAM on both datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SharpBalance's accuracy advantage over SAM depends on architecture and evaluation distribution.

record.problems: The claim versions' target outcomes are not directly measured. Several reported comparisons are presented only in figures, without uncertainty values in the supplied text. The theoretical analysis assumes Gaussian data matrices and quadratic objectives, which the authors identify as limitations.
record.rows_left_out: No numeric figure-bar values were transcribed where the supplied text did not provide a recoverable textual value. Figure 7 and Figure 12 describe accuracy bars, but their exact values are not needed for any listed version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization, and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout effects and interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.

Association between magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and training–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Magnitude-aware sharpness is measured, but these comparisons are absent.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: States are assessed against the listed versions; cannot_determine does not deny the observed out-of-scope findings. Accuracy numbers are recoverable from the supplied figure text. No listed-version results require additional rows.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Large-batch versus small-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
The study measures adaptive sharpness and OOD accuracy but does not measure a training-test gap or the version’s magnitude-aware perturbation criterion.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring the resulting test accuracy.

rows.subject: three-member ResNet18 ensemble
rows.operation_detail: Compared ensemble-member sharpness with ensemble diversity measured by prediction variance, DER, and KL divergence across perturbation radii.
rows.measure: Relationship between sharpness and ensemble diversity
rows.value: The text reports that lower sharpness is correlated with lower diversity; the three diversity metrics show consistent trends.
rows.note: Qualitative result; no numeric values are assigned from the figure.
rows.check: The reported sharpness–diversity association is observed, but diversity cannot establish any listed version's effect. Equation (3) does scale perturbations by weight magnitudes.

rows.subject: three-member ResNet18 ensemble
rows.operation_detail: Related diversity and sharpness to ensemble improvement rate and individual-member OOD accuracy across perturbation radii.
rows.measure: Sharpness-diversity trade-off, ensemble improvement rate, and individual-member OOD accuracy
rows.value: The text reports that reducing sharpness lowers diversity and ensemble improvement rate, while improving individual-member OOD accuracy.
rows.note: The result is stated across the plotted perturbation-radius settings; figure values are not transcribed.
rows.check: Individual-member OOD accuracy and ensemble improvement do not measure a training–test gap.

rows.subject: three-member ResNet18 ensemble

rows.note: The text describes the width comparison qualitatively; no figure-only numeric values are assigned.
rows.check: Width changes are evaluated through sharpness, diversity, and ensemble improvement; zero training error and test error beyond interpolation are not reported.
